recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-28593 unless Pharmacy reopens the later MedicationStatement status/adherence model; any future reconsideration should start from FHIR-32060, FHIR-32858, and FHIR-39271 rather than the superseded initial value list alone.
issue_request: FHIR-28593 asked whether MedicationUsage.status was needed and whether its value set should be narrowed. The Published/Persuasive resolution kept the status attribute, clarified that it is the status of the record rather than clinical medication-use status, and initially chose completed, entered-in-error, and unknown.
initial_application: Commit f351511a957fc178e55907a68ff1016e2387aa80 explicitly cited FHIR-28593 and changed the then-active MedicationUsage StructureDefinition, status CodeSystem, examples, and related files to the narrowed completed/entered-in-error/unknown record-status model.
additional_context: Later Published decisions in the same Pharmacy status family superseded the initial value list: FHIR-32060 removed unknown, renamed completed to recorded, and added draft; FHIR-32858 confirmed use of effective[x] and adherence for medication-use scenarios; FHIR-39271 renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while preserving record-status semantics and adherence for taking/not-taking meaning. Those related decisions are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current build-scope source lists MedicationStatement as active, defines MedicationStatement.status as recorded | entered-in-error | draft, states that status represents recording the medication statement, and directs medication taking/adherence semantics to MedicationStatement.adherence.

related_jiras.note: Replaced the initially applied completed/unknown status values with recorded/draft and confirmed the status-value redesign.
Confirmed that medication-use scenarios should be represented through effective[x] and adherence rather than restoring old status codes.
Renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while preserving record-status semantics and adherence for taking/not-taking meaning.
